chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim and Ibn Muskhan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a person in ihram who trod upon the eggs of sandgrouse and crushed them. He said: He sends a male camel as compensation for a number of eggs equal to the number of eggs, from the sheep, just as he sends a male camel for the number of eggs of the ostrich from the camels.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: Person in ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.بَيْضَ الْقَطَا: Eggs of the sandgrouse (a type of bird)
key_terms.يُرْسِلُ الْفَحْلَ: He sends a male camel (as compensation)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for crushing sandgrouse eggs while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar details the specific fidya for crushing sandgrouse eggs, prescribing the release of a male camel (fahl) as compensation. The ruling draws a direct analogy to the compensation for ostrich eggs, illustrating the juristic method of qiyas in determining the value of game based on species and size within the Shia tradition.
